Avar

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Akin to Andi суни (suni).

Adverb

[edit]

сон • (son)

  1. yesterday

Etymology 2

[edit]

Akin to Budukh сан (san) and Lak шин (šin) and Udi усен (usen).

Noun

[edit]

сон • (son)

  1. year

Erzya

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Mordvinic *son, inherited from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sᴕ̈. Related to Moksha сон (son), Finnish hän, Northern Sami son and possibly Hungarian ő.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /son/

Pronoun

[edit]

сон • (son)

  1. he, she, it (third-person singular)
    • 1910, Makar Evsevievich Evseviev, Gospoda nashego Iisusa Hrista Svyatoe Evangelie ot Matfeya, Marka, Luki i Ioanna na mordovskom yazyke‎[1], page 225:
      Мезть улить, весе Сонзэ кувалт ульсть, Соньтемензэ мезе-як эзь ульть.
      Mezť uľiť, veśe Sonzë kuvalt uľsť, Sońťemenzë meźe-jak eź uľť.
      Through him all things were made; without him nothing was made that has been made.

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sъ̀nъ, from Proto-Indo-European *supnós.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sɔn]
  • Hyphenation: сон
  • Rhymes: -ɔn

Noun

[edit]

сон • (son) m (plural соништа or сништа, relational adjective соновен, diminutive сонче)

  1. dream
  2. sleep

Moksha

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Mordvinic *son, from Proto-Uralic *sᴕ̈. Cognate with Erzya сон (son).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /son/
  • Rhymes: -on
  • Hyphenation: сон

Pronoun

[edit]

сон • (son)

  1. (third person singular) he, she, it
    • (2005), Apostolhńeń ťevsna [Acts of the Apostles], Helsinki: Bibľijäń jotaftoma insťitutś [Institute for Bible Translation]
      Тейст Сон эвондакшнесь нильгемонь шинь кувалма крёз лангса муцендамдонза меле. Иисус ламоксть верондафтозь няфтезе – Сон меки шиса: синь Сонь няезь и Сон азондсь тейст Шкаень Оцязорксшить колга.
      Ťejst Son evondakšńeś ńiľgemoń šiń kuvalma kŕoz langsa mućendamdonza meľe. Ijisus lamoksť verondaftoź ń[ä/a]fťeźe – Son meki šisa: śiń Soń ń[ä/a]jeź i Son azondś ťejst Škajeń Oć[ä/a]zorksšiť kolga.
      He had shown himself alive to them after his Passion by many demonstrations: for forty days he had continued to appear to them and tell them about the kingdom of God.

[edit]

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak son, from Proto-Slavic *sъnъ. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn сон (son) and Slovak sen.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsɔn]
  • Rhymes: -ɔn
  • Hyphenation: сон

Noun

[edit]

сон (son) m inan (diminutive сончок)

  1. sleep, slumber
  2. dream

instrumental сном (snom) снами (snami)
locative сну / шнє (snu / šnje) снох (snox)
vocative сну / шнє (snu / šnje) сни (sni)

  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “dream”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 93
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “sleep”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 284

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
сон
Wikipedia ru

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • сонъ (son) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sъ̀nъ, from Proto-Indo-European *supnós (whence also гипно́з (gipnóz)).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [son]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -on

Noun

[edit]

сон • (son) m inan (genitive сна, nominative plural сны, genitive plural снов)

  1. sleep
  2. dream (imaginary events seen in the mind while sleeping)
    • 1916—1922, Александр Грин (Alexander Grin), Алые паруса [Scarlet sails], filmed in 1961:
      Далеко́-далеко́ отсю́да я уви́дел тебя́ во сне́.
      Dalekó-dalekó otsjúda ja uvídel tebjá vo sné.
      Far, far away from here I saw you in (my) dream.

Yakut

[edit]
Yakut Wikipedia has an article on:
сон
Wikipedia sah

Etymology

[edit]

From Tungusic. Other Turkic languages, as well as Mongolian and Russian, use terms cognate with English paletot.

Noun

[edit]

сон • (son)

  1. (clothing) coat
    эр соно ― er sono ― men's coat
    дьахтар соно ― jaqtar sono ― women's coat
    кыһыҥҥы сон ― kïhïŋŋï son ― winter coat
    халтаҥ сон ― qaltaŋ son ― demi-season coat
    түүлээх сон ― tüüleeq son ― fur coat
